page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.c6 family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The underlying virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the ecs.c6.xlarge in the lower tiers across most metrics. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (1310.68) and multi-core (3484.23) CPU performance fall within the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests indicate weak throughput, with read-only large block operations at 26.23 GB/sec and write large block operations at 22.85 GB/sec. While Geekbench single-core scores register in the average range at 1166.0, the multi-core score of 2549.0 and software compilation score of 3461.0 remain in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET performance (3.38 million operations per second) also align with the bottom 25% of tested instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6.xlarge offers an entry-level compute-optimized profile with dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding the resource contention of shared-core models. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak benchmark results suggest a tradeoff where compute density is prioritized over raw processing speed or memory capacity. This instance is suitable for workloads with moderate CPU requirements that do not demand high memory footprints, such as lightweight web serving, basic text processing, or small-scale utility applications.
